question: According to Joule’s law of heating, if the current flowing through a resistor is doubled while resistance and time remain constant, then the heat produced (H) will increase by a factor of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joule's Law of Heating** describes the rate at which resistance in an electrical circuit converts electrical energy into **heat energy**.
 
• The mathematical expression for Joule's law is **H = I²Rt**, where **H** represents the heat produced, **I** is the electric current, **R** is the resistance of the conductor, and **t** is the time for which the current flows.
 
• According to the law, the **heat produced (H)** is **directly proportional to the square of the current (I²)** flowing through the resistor.
 
• If the current is **doubled** (from **I** to **2I**), the new heat produced becomes **H' = (2I)² * R * t**, which simplifies to **H' = 4 * I² * R * t**.
 
• Comparing the new heat to the original, **H' = 4H**. Therefore, the heat produced increases by a **factor of four** when the current is doubled and other factors remain constant. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **James Prescott Joule**: The law is named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**, who studied the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer in the **1840s**.
 
• **SI Unit of Heat**: The standard **SI unit** for heat and energy is the **Joule (J)**. One Joule is equal to the work done by a force of one newton acting through a distance of one meter.
 
• **Practical Applications**:
 
 
• **Electric Heaters and Irons**: These devices use high-resistance coils to maximize the **heat produced** via Joule heating.
 
• **Electric Bulbs**: The filament (usually **Tungsten**) is heated to such a high temperature by the current that it begins to glow and emit light.
 
• **Electric Fuse**: A safety device that protects circuits from **overloading**. When the current exceeds a certain limit, the heat produced melts the **fuse wire**, breaking the circuit.
 
 
 
• **Dependence on Resistance**: For a constant current and time, the heat produced is directly proportional to the **resistance (R)**. If resistance is doubled, the heat is also doubled.
 
• **Dependence on Time**: Heat produced is directly proportional to the **duration (t)** of current flow. Extending the time the appliance is "on" linearly increases the total heat generated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relationship with Power**: Electrical **Power (P)** is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is dissipated as heat, expressed as **P = H / t = I²R**.
 
• **Ohm’s Law Integration**: By substituting **V = IR** (Ohm’s Law) into the heating formula, heat can also be expressed as **H = VIt** or **H = (V² / R) * t**, where **V** is the potential difference.
 
• **Energy Conservation**: Joule heating is an illustration of the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, where electrical energy is transformed into **thermal energy**.
 
• **Unwanted Heating**: In many electronic components like **computers and transformers**, Joule heating is considered a "loss" of energy and can cause damage if not managed by cooling fans or **heat sinks**.
